# The cloud container

**container**
: Virtual machine with its own disk, on which a cloud session of Claude Code runs. It holds a clone of the branch that the session was created from.

**curator**
: Person in charge of this restoration.

**main session**
: Top-level session of a container, which the curator talks to. The agents that it launches are not main sessions.

**coordinating session**
: Main session that keeps the project's files under `explorations/coordinator/` and launches the workers.

**process stop**
: End of the session's Claude Code process, by the platform's cap, by idleness or by a VM restart. The platform starts the process again in the same session.

**VM restart**
: Restart of the container's machine under a live session.

**check-in**
: One-shot reminder, armed with `send_later`, that wakes the main session with a message at a set time.

**Stop hook**
: Command that Claude Code runs at the end of every turn of the main session.

The platform stops the session's process about every 13 hours and when the session goes idle. It can restart the VM, sometimes with the disk rolled back, and it can lose the container. Running agents survive none of these.

## Rules for every agent

- Before a long run, read the room left on the disk as `references/machine.md` says.
- If your brief lets you push, push your work as you go, as `fortress-repo`'s `references/committing.md` says. Only what is pushed survives a rollback of the disk or a lost container.
- After a process stop, a VM restart or a lost container, run `git status` and `git log origin/<branch>..<branch>` in each tree that you work in, before you start anything again.
- The platform's git-check Stop hook can still ask the main session to commit and push on a turn that the git-check switch misses (`references/hooks.md`). Treat its reminders as advisory. Never commit or push unready work to answer one.

## The parts

- `references/machine.md`, for every agent: the machine, timings across sessions, agents at once, the disk allowance and a full disk, the blocked hosts.
- `references/stops.md`, for every agent: the kinds of process stop and their signs, a disk rolled back, the weekly usage limit, what a stop keeps here. Its section on check-ins is for the coordinating session.
- `references/hooks.md`, for the coordinating session: the transcript backup and its blind spots, the git-check hook and how it is turned off.
- `references/container-loss.md`, for the coordinating session: re-provisioning, re-arming the backup, reading another session's transcript, recovering the work.

How a Claude Code session behaves anywhere (the Bash tool, long commands, waits and the prompt cache, interrupts, the automatic permission check) is `fortress-repo`'s `references/session.md`. Running agents and resuming a run are the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`.

`references/sources.md` gives the source of each fact in these parts. Use it only to maintain this skill. Do not load it for a task.

# The machine and the network

## The machine

- 4 CPUs (Intel Xeon, at 2.1 or 2.8 GHz, which differs between sessions), about 15 GB of memory, and no swap. `nproc`, `free -g` and `/proc/cpuinfo` read them.
- Compare no absolute seconds across sessions: the same work has run 40 % slower in another session.
- A Workflow run starts at most two agents at a time on this machine. The others wait for a free slot. Two agents that build share the four cores.

## The disk allowance

`df -h /` misleads. Its Size column is the whole disk, about 250 GB, and most of it is reserved and cannot be written. The session may use Used plus Avail, about 37 GB, and Use% is taken of that sum. Read the Avail column: it is what is left.

- When the allowance is full, tool output fails with "no space left on device". Check Avail before a long run, and before you seed worktrees or copy builds.
- Temporary files that the work never deletes fill it. In this repository, they are mostly the parser's folders in `/tmp`. `fortress-repo`'s `references/build-and-caches.md` gives their sweep.
- When it is full, stop your own background processes (`fortress-repo`'s `references/session.md`). Delete what you made and no longer need: scratch, build output, private caches, and finished worktrees whose commits are pushed.
- If that is not enough, commit and push, and report that this session's allowance is spent. A new session starts on a fresh machine.

## The network

Outbound HTTPS goes through the session's proxy, which blocks some hosts. `web.archive.org` resets the connection, and the proxy refuses `labs.oracle.com`.

- If you need a research PDF from these hosts, name it in your report. Only the curator can upload it into the session.
- To read an archived page that is not a PDF, fetch it through the pure.md reader relay: `https://pure.md/https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>if_/<url>`. The `if_` after the timestamp is required.

Under a declaring type an overload must now take `self` first (`StaticNativeApp.java:147`, `:154`). - `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/` (`NativeApp.java`, `StaticNativeApp.java`);

- `explorations/`.

No checker code changes, so there is no speed pass.

The ladder subset is empty, so none ran: no recorded first error names code that this rung touched. `grep -iE "StaticNativeApp|NativeApp|FunctionClosure|MethodClosure|FunctionalMethod|Native helper|builtinPrimitive|interpreter" explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/ladder.tsv` prints seven rows:

Every call of the loader is in `FunctionClosure.java` (`:47`, `:52`, `:57`, `:64`, `:69`, `:78`), each reached from a closure:
- The five other `new FunctionClosure(` sites (`BuildEnvironments.java:417`, `Evaluator.java:569`, `BuildLetEnvironments.java:67`, `FGenericFunction.java:99`, `ForeignComponentWrapper.java:67`) and `ClosureInstance` (`FGenericFunction.java:98`) are functions, with no `self`.
- `FunctionClosure(TraitMethod, Environment)` (`:76-81`) passes a definition that the loader has already loaded.

The precedent is climb batch 23's loader (`640acb4a1`), which refuses a declared type that no Java type carries. Its file has two other sites where a declared type meets the carrier table: the parameters (`StaticNativeApp.java:124-131`) and the result (`:132-136`). Both already refuse. `self` was the third, and is now checked (`:137-141`) with the same message form, 'no Java type carries ...'. The library has no precedent for checking a method's receiver: the glue classes are not checked at all (`interpreter/glue/NativeMeth.java:29-31`, the team's comment).

The ways the tree offers, before the choice:

1. The closure tells the loader the declaring type. Taken; this is fork 4.
2. A refusal at the call, in `unbox` (`StaticNativeApp.java:225-234`), where the value is not of the Java type's class. Not taken: row 847 asks for a refusal at load.
3. The declaring type read from the syntax tree. Not taken: the tree has no parent links (fork 4).
4. One table shared with the parameter carry, `javaFor`. Not taken: rung F changes it (fork 4).
5. The declaring type by identity, not by name. Two forms, neither taken:
   - The declaring component read from the declaration's span. This depends on the source path, and a library file shadowed from the current directory, as in the controls below, has another path.
   - A comparison with the type that `Driver.getFortressLibrary()` binds under the name. This depends on the order in which the library's components and types are built, since the library's own methods are loaded while its environments are being built.

## What the specification settles

The specification typesets `builtinPrimitive`'s comment (`Specification/library/default-libraries.tex:37-39`, from `FortressBuiltin.fsi:14-29`). It says two things:
- the interpreter takes "the one whose Java parameter and result types carry the declared types, %self% first";
- "A string under com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers that names no such method is an error on both."

The rung makes the first true of `self`: a method's binding takes an overload with `self` first, at the carrier of the declaring type, and no other. The comment does not say when the error is raised. Row 847's fix asks for the load, and row 864 records where walk raises it later. `grep -rn "self" Specification/library/default-libraries.tex | grep -i "native\|builtinPrimitive"` prints nothing: no other passage speaks of a native's `self`.

## Programs run on the old code and the new

Each probe is a program in the worktree's scratch. New code runs with `bin/fortress`; old code runs with `explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base23 <tree>/tmp/rung-natives-self/old-caches`.

**Row 847's shapes.** On the base, by `bin/fortress` before the edit:
- a trait's dotted method: '6', rc=0;
- a trait's functional method: '6', rc=0;
- a generic object's method: 'before' / '11', rc=0 (11 is the length of `Box[\ZZ32\]`).

On the fix each is refused:

**A program's own type named after each name in the carrier table**, written as `object T` with `len(): ZZ32` bound to `nativeStrlen`:
- `Int`, `String`, `Boolean`, `RR32`, `Float`, `ZZ32`, `NN32`, `Char`, `ZZ64`, `NN64`, `RR64`, `ZZ`, `Long`, `UnsignedLong` and `BigNum`: each rc=255, 'Type name may refer to: Int, FortressBuiltin.Int' (or `FortressLibrary.` for the library's types);
- `FlatString` and `JavaString`: rc=0, '10', on the patch's build. Hence the second change.

**Controls of the self-first rule, with a library binding changed for one run.** No program can declare a method in a type that the table carries, so the rule's other branches can be seen only through the library. Each control:
1. copies `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss` into a scratch directory;
2. changes `Int`'s `getter asString()` binding there (`FortressBuiltin.fss:370-371`);

The library itself is not edited.

| binding of `Int.asString` | old code | new code |
|---|---|---|
| `simpleLongArith.longToString(long)`, `self` at another carried type | 'asString: 5', rc=0 | 'Native helper com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleLongArith.longToString has no overload that fits the declaration's types.', rc=1 |
| `simpleOverload.bar()`, no `self` | 'Native public static java.lang.String com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.bar() given 1 arguments', a `ProgramError` at the call, rc=1 | 'Native helper com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.bar has no overload that fits the declaration's types.', at load, rc=1 |

The second row is the first change's case. By reading, the patch as written (`off == 1 && xs[0] != selfJava`) loads it and fails at the call, as the old code does; this was not measured on a build of the patch alone. The new column was run again on the final code, with the same results.

## Each declaring type the table carries, and the library's bindings

`javaForSelf` carries `self` for fifteen names, each a type of `FortressLibrary` or `FortressBuiltin`:
- in `int`: `ZZ32`, `NN32`, `Char` and `Int`;
- in `long`: `ZZ64`, `NN64`, `Long` and `UnsignedLong`;
- in `double`: `RR64` and `Float`;
- in `float`: `RR32`;
- in `boolean`: `Boolean`;
- in `String`: `String`;
- in `BigInteger`: `ZZ` and `BigNum`.

It carries no other name; `FlatString`, `JavaString` and `()` are among those left out.

It would refuse no library binding:
- **On this tree:** the 21 bindings that name a helper load (the suites; `NativeHelperFamilyZZ32Walk`, `NativeHelperBindingWalk`).
- **For the merged tree, by reading signatures:** I compared the helpers' Java signatures (`javap -public` of `ProjectFortress/build/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/*.class`) against the planner's table of the batch's bindings (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-24/probes/families-base.tsv`: families F, Z, S, K and H, 152 bindings) and climb batch 23's 21 (`moved-base.tsv`). That is 173 bindings. 172 of them are methods of `Float`, `ZZ64`, `ZZ`, `Long`, `NN32`, `BigNum`, `Char`, `NN64`, `ZZ32` and `Int`, and each has an overload whose first Java parameter is its type's carrier. The 12 dotted ones (the getters of `Float`, `Long`, `BigNum`, `Char`, `NN32` and `Int`) each name a helper with one parameter more than the declaration, so the first change skips none of them.
- **The planner's runs:** the planner ran the patch with F, Z and S, and with H, and every binding loaded (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-24.md:409`, `:415`). The two changes refuse only cases that those runs could not contain. K's two `CHOOSE` bindings were in neither run; their helpers take `int` and `long` first.

The gate on the merged tree is the run that confirms this.

## Sentences made false

- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4493-4498`, in the entry "A native binding that names a static helper", Effect: "The interpreter reads the \KWD{self} of a method only by the helper's Java type, since it is not told the type that declares the method: a helper bound in a method of a type that no Java type carries, as a program's own object, is not refused, and its call passes the object as that Java type reads it, the name of its type to a helper over \TYP{String} (row~847 of the revival's gap ledger)." - **rung-W.patch, taken with two changes:** the self-first rule under a declaring type (`StaticNativeApp.java:147`, `:154`), and no carrier for `FlatString` and `JavaString` (`StaticNativeApp.java:88`), for the reasons above.

## Decisions

1. **The planner's text, with two changes.** Ways not taken: the text as it is, which loads a dotted method's helper without `self` under a declaring type (the control's second row) and a program's own `FlatString` or `JavaString` (the name probes, '10'); a reworked mechanism, of which the patch's is fork 4's default.

Evidence: the controls; none of the merged batch's 12 dotted bindings has such a helper.
3. **`FlatString` and `JavaString` carry no `self`**, by name. Ways not taken: keeping both, which leaves row 847's symptom for two names; an identity check of the declaring type, by its declaration's file or against the library's environment, which is heavier and depends on the source path or on the order of loading (way 5 above); leaving out only `JavaString`. 4. **Tests over every constructor that a program reaches**, each read off the stack trace: the object and trait cases (`MethodClosure`'s first), the functional case (`FunctionalMethod`'s first), the generic case (`FunctionalMethod`'s second), the two names, and row 864's home-3 test. No program reaches `MethodClosure`'s second constructor with a type that no Java type carries (above).
5. **The promoted test's key names the helper and the refusal.** Way not taken: the `XXX` file's key, the helper's name only, which a refusal for another reason ('has no overload that fits') would also satisfy.
6. **The rule's other branches shown by controls on a shadowed `FortressBuiltin.fss`, not by gated tests**, because no program can declare a method in a carried type. Ways not taken: an edit of `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/` for one run, which the brief's file list excludes; no control.
7. **Row 864 recorded, not fixed:** home 3, since the specification is silent on when the error is raised. Ways not taken: a check of a generic type's helper bindings where the type is declared, which lies outside the rung's files (`BuildEnvironments.java` or `FTypeGeneric.java`); home 2, which needs the specification to settle the timing.
8. **No stage, no ladder subset, no demos run:** the paths (forks 10 and 8) and the subset's grep, above.
9. **Both suites run again after the second change**, which made a new code state. The first state's runs are kept above as superseded.

- **Row 864**, a dotted method of a generic trait or object is refused only at its instance: home 3, with `NativeHelperUncarriedSelfGenericObjectWalk` (it loads while no instance is made) and the row in `record.md`.

## For FACTS

See `record.md`: F-299 rewritten, with its row-847 sentence replaced by the check of `self`.

## Commands

- The constructor a refusal passes through: `cd ProjectFortress && ../bin/fortress -debug stacktrace tests/<name>.fss 2>&1 | grep -n "FunctionalMethod.<init>\|MethodClosure.<init>\|TraitMethod.<init>"`.

For the old code, run it through `old-fortress.sh` from the same directory.
- The helpers' Java signatures: `javap -cp ProjectFortress/build -public com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.<Class>`.

None blocks the landing. One question is left open for the batch that moves `FlatString`'s bindings: whether the loader should then identify the declaring type by its declaration rather than by its name (decision 3; `StaticNativeApp.java:88`).

### Where the text, the brief or the principles split

**1. Way 2b checks a composition, and the transfers are identities (rung H; Question 2).** P-58: "from the step that moves a binding, the compiled checker checks it against the helper's Java signature" (`POSITIONS.md:55`). For H's 76, the checker reads the helper's call wrapped in the transfers, each of which returns its argument (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleUnsignedIntArith.java:230-231`). So the composition passes whatever the helper computes. Skeptic H's program shows it: a binding over `NN32` named to the signed `simpleIntArith.intLT` is refused on the old code ("(ZZ32, ZZ32)->Boolean is not applicable to an argument of type (NN32, NN32)"), and compiles and answers `true` for 2^31 < 1 on the new code; "So a loud static error becomes a quiet value" (`compile-ladder/rung-natives-hard/SKEPTIC.md:112-134`). Walk answers the same (F-299). For the 76, the walk and compiled guards check that each names the unsigned helper, and they do (F-308). For a later binding over these types, only its guard will. The record's Question 2 weighs the four ways by the team's word and the library's form (`CLIMB-BATCH-24.md:90-100`), and the probe by the same and by distance runs (`plan-24/probes/hard-set.md`, sections 4 to 7); neither names this cost. Question 2 was taken at the probe's default under his half-hour rule, "On his review list" (`:92`). Default: as landed. No entry holds it yet (finding 2).

**2. A compile-time refusal became a run-time crash (rung G; row 867; G.skeptic.1).** On the base, the code generator refused a function or method whose own `where` clause introduces a `where`-clause variable, 'Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl.'. With the guard's condition gone, it compiles and links, and its compiled call dies with `NoClassDefFoundError` (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXWhereVariableCallCompiled.fss:16-21`). The skeptic asks whether to keep refusing that form until the template carries the variable (`PLAN.md:656`). Default: as landed, the deferred `XXX` run pair. A loud failure stays loud, but moves from the compile to the run.

**3. The code generator compiles every header `where` clause, beyond P-151's three forms (rung G; fork 12).** P-151: "Only the `where`-clause forms that the team wrote down are built: conditional extension, a function's or a method's condition, and `AnyList`'s `comprises` clause" (`POSITIONS.md:63`). G dropped the condition at all three guards, so an object's or a trait's own `where` clause on its own static parameters compiles too (`CodeGen.java:4103-4111`, `:5022-5027`; `compiler_tests/WhereBoundObjectCompiled.fss`). The checker already reads an object's own constraint (`.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/compiler.md:103`), and the code generator emits nothing for any clause, so no new form gets semantics; G's decision 3 says so (`compile-ladder/rung-codegen-where/REPORT.md`, "9. Decisions", 3). Fork 12's default, not consequential by the record (`CLIMB-BATCH-24.md:117`). A reading of P-151's "built" at the code generator, routine, on the forks' item.

**4. Walk reads a method's declaring type by its name (rung W).** The loader takes `self`'s carrier from the declaring type's name, for fifteen types whose names no program can give its own types, and gives `FlatString` and `JavaString` no carrier, since a program can name its types so (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:81-95`). W improved the planner's text there: on the patch's build, a program's own `object FlatString` with a helper bound to `nativeStrlen` answered 10 (`rung-natives-self/REPORT.md:27`). The cost is item 63: a library binding of a `FlatString` method that names a helper would stop every program at load (`PLAN.md:145`; skeptic W, "For the curator"). Two departures stay, each with its home: a dotted method of a generic trait or object is refused only where an instance's method is made (row 864), and a program's object that extends a carried trait against its `comprises` clause still reaches the helper (row 551; F-299). No default on record for item 63.

**5. The comment's "rewrites the body", and a local function (row 865).** The revised comment says "The compiler, before type checking, rewrites the body into a call of the helper" (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:19`). The rewrite reaches a component's declarations and its traits' and objects' members only (`BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java:54-86`), so a helper string in a local function or an object expression's method stops 'Variable builtinPrimitive is not defined.', where walk answers (row 865). The gather named it among the Effect's departures (`changes.tex`, the Effect of "A native binding that names a static helper"). The manual's rule 4 asks the departing path "a gated XXX test asserting the text's rule" (`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "Rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect", 4); the row has reproducer `none`, its test owed as review-routed.1 (`PLAN.md:659`). Climb batch 23's row 849 met the same rule (its finding 8). No library binding sits in either form.

**6. A floating-point division by zero: NaN or infinity (rung F; row 863).** "For floating-point results, division by zero produces a NaN value according to the rules of IEEE 754." (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:167-168`). #!/bin/bash
# seed-worktree.sh <base-worktree> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]
#
# Makes a worktree that is ready to compile and run Fortress without building anything, by copying the
# build and the caches of a baseline worktree that has been built once, and translating the parts of the
# caches that are keyed by the source tree's absolute path (explorations/coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md).
#
#   <base-worktree>  a clean worktree of this repository at some commit B, on which `ant compileAll` and the
#                    library-order recompile (explorations/repo-internals.md, "Compile order matters") have
#                    run, and nothing since.
#   <new-worktree>   where the new worktree goes; made by `git worktree add`, reused if it already exists.
#   <branch>         the branch it checks out: an existing local branch, else origin's, else a new branch
#                    cut from <start-point>, which defaults to B; `-` makes a detached worktree at
#                    <start-point> instead. Old-against-new runs need no copy of the base: tools/old-fortress.sh
#                    runs the base build itself with a private caches folder.
#
# What it does, in order: adds the worktree; copies ProjectFortress/build, ProjectFortress/.dependencies
# and default_repository/caches from the base; renames every file of the AST caches (analyzed_cache,
# interpreter_cache, interpreter_parsed_cache) to the hash of its source's new path (NamingCzar.deCaseName,
# compiler/NamingCzar.java:244-245; GraphNode.java:33 hashes the canonical path) and rewrites the base path
# inside it; rewrites the base path in the bytecode-cache jars' SourceFile attributes (debug information
# only: jars copied unchanged also run, but their stack traces would name the base's files); and makes the
# new worktree the base's replica in its file dates too. The copies keep the base's dates (cp -a), every
# tracked file whose content is the base's takes the base file's date, and every tracked file that differs
# from B, committed or not, is stamped later than everything copied. Dates decide three things. The
# repository uses a cached entry only when it is not older than its source (repository/GraphRepository.java:244,
# :283; a changed api also makes everything that imports it stale, :600-620). Ant regenerates the AST
# nodes, the parsers and Operators.java when an input is newer than the generated file (build.xml:371-384,
# :450-467, :1335-1400); the checkout's own dates make it regenerate them, and javac then recompiles 1,077
# files. And javac recompiles a source newer than its class (build-cache-exploration.md, section 6). So the
# next `fortress compile` of a differing library source rebuilds it, and a worktree whose ProjectFortress/src
# differs from B is seeded with a warning: the copied build is B's, so the worker runs ant compileAll, which
# recompiles the differing sources (and deletes the caches, build.xml:715 and :356), and the library-order
# recompile before its first compiled run. The base's own dates must be a build's: a base built in place by
# ant, or seeded by this script.
#
# A worktree that already has ProjectFortress/build is left alone (a relaunch keeps the worker's own build);
# SEED_FORCE=1 replaces its build and caches with the base's.
#
# Prints one line per step with its time, and the seeded worktree's path last. Exits non-zero, having
